Exclusions

First remove the non-italian speaking participants

d <- df %>% 
  filter(!Participant %in% non_its$Participant) %>% 
  filter(!Participant %in% low_reading$Participant)

# How many people were removed?
length(unique(df$Participant)) - length(unique(d$Participant))
## [1] 83
# How many people reamining?
length(unique(d$Participant))/length(unique(df$Participant))*100
## [1] 69.59707
length(unique(d$Participant))
## [1] 190
d$likert_valence <- ordered(d$likert_valence)
d$likert_arousal <- ordered(d$likert_arousal)
d$val_num <- as.numeric(d$likert_valence)
d$ar_num  <- as.numeric(d$likert_arousal)
d <- d %>%
  mutate(
    Nativeness.n = ifelse(Nativeness == "L1", 0, 1),
    val_c = scale(val_num, scale = FALSE),
    ar_c  = scale(ar_num, scale = FALSE)
  )

#Ordinal bad

model.ord <- glm(
  Nativeness.n ~ likert_valence * likert_arousal,
  data = d,
  family = binomial
)

numeric good

model.num <- glm(
  Nativeness.n ~ val_num * ar_num,
  family = binomial,
  data = d
)

summary(model.num)
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = Nativeness.n ~ val_num * ar_num, family = binomial, 
##     data = d)
## 
## Coefficients:
##                Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)    -0.55364    0.14770  -3.748 0.000178 ***
## val_num         0.24731    0.02322  10.651  < 2e-16 ***
## ar_num          0.28094    0.02647  10.613  < 2e-16 ***
## val_num:ar_num -0.04802    0.00412 -11.656  < 2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1)
## 
##     Null deviance: 5914.6  on 4965  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 5771.5  on 4962  degrees of freedom
## AIC: 5779.5
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 4
anova(model.ord, model.num, test = "Chisq")
## Analysis of Deviance Table
## 
## Model 1: Nativeness.n ~ likert_valence * likert_arousal

centered best

)

sapply(model.frame(model.c), class)
## $Nativeness.n
## [1] "numeric"
## 
## $val_c
## [1] "matrix" "array" 
## 
## $ar_c
## [1] "matrix" "array"
# refit the model with numeric vectors
# ensure numeric consistency
d$val_c <- as.numeric(d$val_c)
d$ar_c  <- as.numeric(d$ar_c)

model.c <- glm(
  Nativeness.n ~ val_c * ar_c,
  family = binomial,
  data = d
)

# prediction grid
newdata <- expand.grid(
  val_c = seq(min(d$val_c, na.rm = TRUE),
              max(d$val_c, na.rm = TRUE),
              length.out = 100),
  ar_c  = seq(min(d$ar_c, na.rm = TRUE),
              max(d$ar_c, na.rm = TRUE),
              length.out = 100)
)

# THIS STEP MUST SUCCEED
newdata$prob_L2 <- predict(model.c, newdata, type = "response")

ggplot(newdata, aes(x = val_c, y = ar_c, fill = prob_L2)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "C") +
  scale_color_manual(values = vaPalette) +
  labs(
    title = "Predicted Probability of L2",
    x = "Centered Valence",
    y = "Centered Arousal",
    fill = "P(L2)"
  )

ggplot() +

  # 1. probability surface
  geom_tile(data = newdata,
            aes(x = val_c, y = ar_c, fill = prob_L2),
            alpha = 0.9) +

  # 2. contour lines (structure of interaction)
  geom_contour(data = newdata,
               aes(x = val_c, y = ar_c, z = prob_L2),
               breaks = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75),
               color = "white",
               linewidth = 0.4) +

  # 3. decision boundary (key interpretive line)
  geom_contour(data = newdata,
               aes(x = val_c, y = ar_c, z = prob_L2),
               breaks = 0.5,
               color = "black",
               linewidth = 0.8) +

  # 4. observed data points
  geom_point(data = d,
             aes(x = val_c, y = ar_c, color = Nativeness),
             alpha = 0.35,
             size = 1.5) +

  # 5. color scales
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colors = c("#F54927", "white", "#3C91E6")
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = vaPalette) +

  # 6. labels
  labs(
    title = "Interaction of Valence and Arousal Predicting Nativeness",
    x = "Centered Valence",
    y = "Centered Arousal",
    fill = "P(L2)",
    color = "Observed Nativeness"
  ) +

  # 7. clean theme
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

newdata <- expand.grid(
  val_c = seq(min(d$val_c, na.rm = TRUE),
              max(d$val_c, na.rm = TRUE),
              length.out = 250),
  ar_c  = seq(min(d$ar_c, na.rm = TRUE),
              max(d$ar_c, na.rm = TRUE),
              length.out = 250)
)

newdata$prob_L2 <- predict(model.c, newdata, type = "response")

Are they more extreme or varied?

✔ L2 has significantly higher absolute deviation from the mean on valence ✔ L2 distribution is more spread out ✔ Same direction, but weaker effect

d$val_extreme <- abs(scale(d$val_num, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE))
d$ar_extreme  <- abs(scale(d$ar_num, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE))

t.test(val_extreme ~ Nativeness, data = d)
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  val_extreme by Nativeness
## t = 6.1007, df = 2696.9, p-value = 1.208e-09
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group L1 and group L2 is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  0.1649071 0.3211240
## sample estimates:
## mean in group L1 mean in group L2 
##         2.897702         2.654687
t.test(ar_extreme ~ Nativeness, data = d)
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  ar_extreme by Nativeness
## t = -3.2359, df = 2476.5, p-value = 0.001229
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group L1 and group L2 is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -0.22551716 -0.05532683
## sample estimates:
## mean in group L1 mean in group L2 
##         1.903929         2.044351
var(d$val_num[d$Nativeness == "L1"])
## [1] 9.951254
var(d$val_num[d$Nativeness == "L2"])
## [1] 8.770368
p2 <- ggplot(d, aes(x = Nativeness, y = val_extreme, fill = Nativeness)) +

  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, outlier.alpha = 0.2) +

  scale_fill_manual(values = c("L1" = "#F54927", "L2" = "#3C91E6")) +

  labs(
    title = "B. Valence Extremity by Nativeness",
    x = "",
    y = "Absolute Deviation from Mean Valence"
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        panel.grid = element_blank())

p2

d_long <- d %>%
  select(Nativeness, val_extreme, ar_extreme) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = c(val_extreme, ar_extreme),
                      names_to = "measure",
                      values_to = "value")


p2 <- ggplot(d_long, aes(x = Nativeness, y = value, fill = Nativeness)) +
